newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan overnight rates rise to 8.50-9.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Jordan overnight rates rise to 8.50-9.50 pct.

text.p: Overnight rates on the Jordanian dinar rose again on Thursday to 8.50-9.50 percent from Wednesday's 8.00 to 9.00 percent after the Central Bank pulled more funds out of the market, dealers said.
Rates soared on Wednesday to the 5.0-percent from the 3.00-percent range, where they were stuck for more than a week.
"I guess the Central Bank withdrew money from the market," said one banker. "When the market goes lower, the Central Bank seems to step in," he said.

Bankers said the Central Bank might be keen to hoist overnight rates to give banks incentive to hunt for longer-term deposits from clients, increasing the amount of dinar-held accounts and resisting any slip towards dollarisation.
With overnight rates so low, the banks had little motive to borrow money long-term at higher rates, they said.
Another banker said the size of the overnight market meant a few million dinars withdrawn could make the difference between three-percent and 10-percent rates.
He said the market was expected to remain fairly tight when it reopened on Sunday, but liquidity would depend on subscription to Saturday's Certificate of Deposit offering.
